d.t: (uncountable) A dessert made from frozen sweetened cream or a similar substance, usually flavoured.
d.e: Strawberries are particularly delicious with ice cream.

d.t: (countable) A portion of ice cream on a stick, in a cup or in a wafer cone.
d.e: Can I have some money for an ice cream, Mum?

d.t: (slang, uncountable) The drug methamphetamine.
(philosophy) An abstract archetype of a given thing, compared to which real-life examples are seen as imperfect approximations; pure essence, as opposed to actual examples.
(obsolete) The conception of someone or something as representing a perfect example; an ideal.
(obsolete) The form or shape of something; a quintessential aspect or characteristic.
An image of an object that is formed in the mind or recalled by the memory.
d.e: The mere idea of you is enough to excite me.

d.t: More generally, any result of mental activity; a thought, a notion; a way of thinking.
A conception in the mind of something to be done; a plan for doing something, an intention.
d.e: I have an idea of how we might escape.

d.t: A purposeful aim or goal; intent.
d.e: Yeah, that's the idea.

d.t: A vague or fanciful notion; a feeling or hunch; an impression.
d.e: He had the wild idea that if he leant forward a little, he might be able to touch the mountain-top.

d.t: (music) A musical theme or melodic subject.
Supposing that, assuming that, in the circumstances that; suppositive used to introduce a condition that may be (or prove to be) either true or false.
d.e: I'll do it next week if I have time.

d.t: Supposing that; used with past or past perfect subjunctive to indicate a counterfactual or hypothetical condition.
d.e: If she hadn't told me, I wouldn't know.

d.t: Considering the fact that; given that; introducing a condition that is known to be true.
d.e: The drain's blocked — and if the drain's blocked, the water won't flow.

d.t: When; whenever; every time that.
d.e: If you heat water to 100° C, it boils.

d.t: Although; used to introduce a concession; may..but.
d.e: He was a great friend, if a little stingy at the bar.

d.t: (literary) While; used to introduce a contrast.
d.e: If tea is expensive, coffee is completely unaffordable.

d.t: (sometimes proscribed) Whether; used to introduce a noun clause, an indirect question, that functions as the direct object of certain verbs.
d.e: I don't know if I want to go or not.

d.t: Introducing a relevance conditional; in case.
d.e: I have leftover cake if you want some.

d.t: (informal) An uncertainty, possibility, condition, doubt etc.
d.e: The board can't approve this project; there are too many ifs.

d.t: Having relevant and crucial value; having import.
d.e: We thought it important for there to be a fire escape at the back of every building.

d.t: (obsolete) Pompous; self-important.
Used to indicate location, inclusion, or position within spatial, temporal or abstract limits.
As to enter; from outside to inside; into.
d.e: Less water gets in your boots this way.

d.t: By (doing something); indicating action causing an effect or achieving a purpose.
d.e: In replacing the faucet washers, he felt he was making his contribution to the environment.

d.t: Indicating an order or arrangement.
d.e: My fat rolls around in folds.

d.t: Denoting a state of the subject.
d.e: He stalked away in anger.

d.t: Indicates, connotatively, a place-like form of someone's (or something's) personality, as his, her or its psychic and physical characteristics.
d.e: You've got a friend in me.

d.t: Pertaining to; with regard to.
d.e: There has been no change in his condition.

d.t: As to have sufficient or plentiful amounts of.
d.e: The fruit trees in the yard keep me in apples and pears for most of the year.

d.t: Used to indicate means, medium, format, genre, or instrumentality.
(obsolete, transitive) To enclose.
(obsolete, transitive) To take in; to harvest.
At or towards the interior of a defined space, such as a building or room.
d.e: Suddenly a strange man walked in.

d.t: Towards the speaker or other reference point.
d.e: They flew in from London last night.

d.t: So as to be enclosed or surrounded by something.
d.e: Bring the water to the boil and drop the vegetables in.

d.t: After the beginning of something.
d.e: The show still didn't become interesting 20 minutes in.

d.t: (in combination, after a verb) Denotes a gathering of people assembled for the stated activity, sometimes, though not always, suggesting a protest.
d.e: sing-in, pray-in, hug-in; see also be-in, love-in, sit-in, teach-in.

d.t: A position of power or influence, or a way to get it.
d.e: His parents got him an in with the company.

d.t: (chiefly in the plural) One who, or that which, is in; especially, one who is in office.
(sports) The state of a batter/batsman who is currently batting; see innings.
Abbreviation of inch or inches.
(not comparable) Located indoors, especially at home or at one's office or place of work.
d.e: Is Mr. Smith in?

d.t: (not comparable) Located inside something.
d.e: Little by little I pushed the snake into the basket, until finally all of it was in.

d.t: (sports, of the ball or other playing implement) Falling or remaining within the bounds of the playing area.
d.e: If the tennis ball bounces on the line then it's in.

d.t: Inserted or fitted into something.
d.e: I've discovered why the TV wasn't working – the plug wasn't in!

d.t: Having been collected or received.
d.e: The replies to the questionnaires are now all in.

d.t: In fashion; popular.
d.e: Skirts are in this year.

d.t: Incoming.
d.e: the in train

d.t: (nautical, of the sails of a vessel) Furled or stowed.
Of the tide, at or near its highest level.
d.e: You can't get round the headland when the tide's in.

d.t: (law) With privilege or possession; used to denote a holding, possession, or seisin.
d.e: in by descent; in by purchase; in of the seisin of her husband

d.t: (cricket) Currently batting.
Having familiarity or involvement with somebody.
d.e: He is very in with the Joneses.

d.t: (law) Resulting from the actions of parties.
(modal) Actually; in truth; de facto.
d.e: People think he's rich, but in fact he's nearly penniless.

d.t: Moreover.
d.e: I don't have the time or patience to deal with him. In fact, I barely even have time for being here at all.

d.t: To bring into a group, class, set, or total as a (new) part or member.
d.e: I will purchase the vacation package if you will include car rental.

d.t: To consider as part of something; to comprehend.
d.e: The vacation package includes car rental.

d.t: (obsolete) To enclose, confine.
(obsolete) To conclude; to terminate.
(programming) To use a directive that allows the use of source code from another file.
d.e: You have to include the strings library to use this function.

d.t: (programming) A piece of source code or other content that is dynamically retrieved for inclusion in another item.
(intransitive) (of a quantity, etc.) To become larger or greater, to greaten.
d.e: His rage only increased when I told him of the lost money.

d.t: (transitive) To make (a quantity, etc.) larger.
To multiply by the production of young; to be fertile, fruitful, or prolific.
(astronomy, intransitive) To become more nearly full; to show more of the surface; to wax.
d.e: The Moon increases.

d.t: An amount by which a quantity is increased.
d.e: An increase of about 30% in hits on the website.

d.t: For a quantity, the act or process of becoming larger.
Offspring, progeny.
(knitting, crochet) The creation of one or more new stitches; see Increase (knitting).
Something that provides a definitive characterization or description of the nature and attributes of a specified entity.
Things that are or can be known about a given topic; communicable knowledge of something.
d.e: I need some more information about this issue.

d.t: The act of informing or imparting knowledge; notification.
d.e: For your information, I did this because I wanted to.

d.t: (law, countable) A statement of criminal activity brought before a judge or magistrate; in the UK, used to inform a magistrate of an offence and request a warrant; in the US, an accusation brought before a judge without a grand jury indictment.
(obsolete) The act of informing against someone, passing on incriminating knowledge; accusation.
(now rare) The systematic imparting of knowledge; education, training.
(now rare) The creation of form; the imparting of a given quality or characteristic; forming, animation.
(computing, formally) The meaning that a human assigns to data by means of the known conventions used in its representation.
(Christianity) Divine inspiration.
A service provided by telephone which provides listed telephone numbers of a subscriber.
(information theory) Any unambiguous abstract data, the smallest possible unit being the bit.
(computing, data management) The output resulting from the systematic collection, manipulation and organization of raw data into a structured, interpretable format.
The interior or inner part.
d.e: The inside of the building has been extensively restored.

d.t: The left-hand side of a road if one drives on the left, or right-hand side if one drives on the right.
d.e: On a motorway, you should never pass another vehicle on the inside.

d.t: The side of a curved road, racetrack etc. that has the shorter arc length; the side of a racetrack nearer the interior of the course or some other point of reference.
d.e: The car in front drifted wide on the bend, so I darted up the inside to take the lead.

d.t: (colloquial, in the plural) The interior organs of the body, especially the guts.
d.e: Eating that stuff will damage your insides.

d.t: (dated, UK, colloquial) A passenger within a coach or carriage, as distinguished from one upon the outside.
(slang) The inside scoop; information known only to certain involved people.
Of or pertaining to the inner surface, limit or boundary.
d.e: The inside surface of the cup is unpainted.

d.t: Nearer to the interior or centre of something.
d.e: Because of the tighter bend, it's harder to run in an inside lane.

d.t: Originating from, arranged by, or being someone inside an organisation.
d.e: The reporter had received inside information about the forthcoming takeover.

d.t: (of a person) Legally married to or related to (e.g. born in wedlock to), and/or residing with, a specified other person (parent, child, or partner); (of a marriage, relationship, etc) existing between two such people.
(baseball, of a pitch) Toward the batter as it crosses home plate.
d.e: The first pitch is ... just a bit inside.

d.t: At or towards or the left-hand side of the road if one drives on the left, or right-hand side if one drives on the right.
d.e: the inside lane of the motorway

d.t: Within or towards the interior of something; within the scope or limits of a place, especially a building.
d.e: I opened the book and found a hidden note inside.

d.t: Intimately, secretly or in one's inner heart or soul; without expressing what one is feeling or thinking.
d.e: That's something I truly believe inside.

d.t: Within the interior of, closest to the center or to a specific point of reference; on the interior side of.
d.e: He placed the letter inside the envelope.

d.t: To the interior of.
d.e: She walked inside the house.

d.t: Within (a period of time).
d.e: The job was finished inside two weeks.

d.t: (uncountable, finance) The price paid for obtaining, or price received for providing, money or goods in a credit transaction, calculated as a fraction of the amount or value of what was borrowed.
d.e: Our bank offers borrowers an annual interest of 5%.

d.t: (uncountable, finance) Any excess over and above an exact equivalent
(uncountable) A great attention and concern from someone or something; intellectual curiosity.
d.e: He has a lot of interest in vintage cars.

d.t: (uncountable) Attention that is given to or received from someone or something.
(often in the plural) Advantage, welfare, or something that serves it.
(countable) An involvement, claim, right, share, stake in or link with a financial, business, or other undertaking or endeavor.
d.e: When scientists and doctors write articles and when politicians run for office, they are required in many countries to declare any existing conflicts of interest (competing interests).

d.t: (countable) Something which, or someone whom, one is interested in.
d.e: Lexicography is one of my interests.

d.t: (uncountable) Condition or quality of exciting concern or being of importance.
(obsolete, rare) Injury, or compensation for injury; damages.
(often in the plural) The persons and companies interested in any particular business or measure, taken collectively.
d.e: the iron interest;  the cotton interest

d.t: (historical, usually attributive) A genre of factual short films, generally more amusing than informative, especially those not covered by a more specific genre label.
d.e: By interest films is meant a variety of subjects which cannot be classified under such recognized headings as fiction, travel, or topical. They include wonderful inventions, little known industries, applied art, feats of engineering, and other events capable of effective illustration.

d.t: To engage the attention of; to awaken interest in; to excite emotion or passion in, in behalf of a person or thing.
d.e: It might interest you to learn that others have already tried that approach.

d.t: (obsolete, often impersonal) To be concerned with or engaged in; to affect; to concern; to excite.
(obsolete) To cause or permit to share.
To or towards the inside of.
d.e: Mary danced into the house.

d.t: To or towards the region of.
d.e: We left the house and walked into the street.

d.t: To the condition or state.
d.e: They lulled us into thinking we still had time.

d.t: Against, especially with force or violence.
d.e: The car crashed into the tree.

d.t: Indicates transition into another form or substance.
d.e: I carved the piece of driftwood into a sculpture of a whale.

d.t: Indicates division or the creation of subgroups or sections.
d.e: A cow's stomach is divided into four chambers.

d.t: After the start of.
d.e: About 20 minutes into the flight, the pilot reported a fire on board.

d.t: (colloquial) Interested in or attracted to.
d.e: She's really heavily into Shakespeare right now.

d.t: (mathematics) Expressing the operation of division, with the denominator given first. Usually with "goes".
d.e: How many times does 24 go into 48?

d.t: (UK, archaic, India, mathematics) Expressing the operation of multiplication.
d.e: Five into three is fifteen.

d.t: Investigating the subject (of).
d.e: There have been calls for research into the pesticides that are blamed for the decline in bee populations.

d.t: (colloquial) Attacking or fighting a person.
d.e: The next time he'll wrestle you, he'll be into you faster than you can say the word sumo.

d.t: The third-person singular neuter personal pronoun used to refer to an inanimate object, abstract entity, or non-human living thing.
d.e: Take this book and put it on the shelf.

d.t: A third-person singular personal pronoun used to refer to a baby or child, especially of unknown gender.
d.e: She took the baby and held it in her arms.

d.t: (rare) A third-person singular pronoun used to refer to an unspecified person.
d.e: All these things inclined her, step by step, to submit to the new discovery, whether Queen Victoria's or another's, that each man and each woman has another allotted to it for life, whom it supports, by whom it is supported, till death them do part.

d.t: (obsolete) An affectionate third-person singular personal pronoun.
d.e:
1897, Olive Pratt Rayner (Grant Allen), The Type-Writer Girl
She caught my eye, and laughed. “What a funny girl it is!” she cried. “You are so comical! But it isn't the least use your trying to frighten me. I can see the twinkle in your big black eyes; and I like you in spite of your trying to be horrid. Do you know, I liked you from the first moment I saw you.”

d.t: (chiefly derogatory, offensive) A third-person singular personal pronoun used to refer to an animate referent who is transgender or non-binary.
d.e:
1977-1980, Lou Sullivan, personal diary, quoted in 2019, Ellis Martin, Zach Ozma (editors), We Both Laughed In Pleasure
Next morning bought her [a drag queen] breakfast & she asked for a couple dollars to get a drink. Gave her $3, walked her to a bar. […] Some teenage boys watched us walking & began shouting. When I left her at the bar door & kissed her goodbye, they began shouting "Ugh! You kissed it!!"

d.t: Refers to someone being identified, often on the phone, but not limited to this situation.
d.e: It's me, John.

d.t: The impersonal pronoun, used without referent as the subject of an impersonal verb or statement (known as the dummy pronoun, dummy it or weather it).
d.e: It is nearly 10 o’clock.

d.t: The impersonal pronoun, used without referent, or with unstated but contextually implied referent, in various short idioms or expressions.
d.e: rough it

d.t: (uncountable) Sex appeal, especially that which goes beyond physical appearance.

The impersonal pronoun, used as a placeholder for a delayed subject, or less commonly, object; known as the dummy pronoun (according to some definitions), anticipatory it or, more formally in linguistics, a syntactic expletive. The delayed subject is commonly a to-infinitive, a gerund, or a noun clause introduced by a subordinating conjunction.
d.e: It’s not worth talking to you.

d.t: All or the end; something after which there is no more.
d.e: Are there more students in this class, or is this it?

d.t: (obsolete) Followed by an omitted and understood relative pronoun: That which; what.
(obsolete) Its.
One who is neither a he nor a she; a creature; a dehumanized being.
The person who chases and tries to catch the other players in the playground game of tag.
d.e: In the next game, Adam and Tom will be it…

d.t: (UK) A game of tag.
d.e: Let's play it at breaktime.

d.t: (informal) A desirable characteristic, as being fashionable.
d.e: Man, he's really got it.

d.t: (informal, chiefly in the negative) Something desirable or suitable.
d.e: Bro, that shirt is not it.

d.t: (informal) Sexual intercourse.
d.e: OMG, they were doing it in the storage room.

d.t: (informal) Sex appeal.
d.e: She really has it going on.

Alternative letter-case form of It (“the id”).
(colloquial) Most fashionable, popular, or in vogue.
